data.title: Cornell faculty senate declares no confidence in university leadership
data.description:
Key points:
  • Vote wins backing from 55.6% of elected faculty senators who cast ballots
  • Resolution carries no binding consequences under Cornell faculty senate procedures
  • Cornell board backs president and administration after vote

By Maria Tsvetkova

Cornell University's faculty senate approved a resolution of no confidence on Friday in the administration's ability to handle what it has called a sexual assault crisis, after a former student sued the university for not protecting her from an alleged 2024 gang rape.

The resolution, which 55.6% of elected faculty senators who cast votes supported, is a condemnation of Cornell's leadership from its major legislative and advisory body, but has no concrete consequences. The tally showed 37% voted against it and 7.4% abstained, Cornell University spokesperson Rebecca Valli said.

"The Faculty Senate has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University," the resolution said.

The former student, who is identified by the pseudonym Jane Doe in court documents, alleged in her civil complaint that Cornell failed to protect her from being raped.

Her lawsuit, filed in September, has also drawn criticism of the university's handling of the case in 2024. Cornell, located in Ithaca, New York, responded that it had conducted a comprehensive investigation and imposed disciplinary measures, including expulsions.

BOARD SUPPORTS PRESIDENT

In response to the resolution, Cornell University Board Chair Anne Smalling expressed the board of trustees' support for University President Michael Kotlikoff and the administration.

"Today’s Faculty Senate vote reflects the deep anger across our campus and sends a clear signal that what happened to Jane Doe is unacceptable," the statement said. "We support President Kotlikoff’s commitment to taking all necessary steps to ensure students are safe on campus and working together as a community to help prevent this from happening again."

Kotlikoff has not responded to the university about the vote outcome, Valli, the university spokesperson, said. Under university procedures, the president has 30 days to respond in writing, she said.

Kotlikoff said the day before voting began on October 29 that faculty discussion and debate were "an important component of Cornell’s shared governance" and that the university had taken measures including adding staff to its civil rights office, expanding sexual assault prevention education, and hiring staff focused on victim advocacy.

Cornell faculty senator Risa Lieberwitz, who co-sponsored the resolution, has said the administration failed to address the sexual assault problem in a systemic way during the more than a decade Kotlikoff has served in senior leadership. Kotlikoff has been Cornell president since March last year.

"Students, faculty, and staff have lost trust that sexual assault cases will be handled properly," Lieberwitz said in an online discussion of the resolution on the Cornell website in late October. "This will have a chilling effect on reporting, creating fear that reporting sexual assault to this administration will be ineffective and even damaging."

Dean of Faculty Chris Schaffer had previously said in a post that he opposed the resolution because it did not "articulate the specific failures underlying its judgment or the consequences it seeks."

"When we make a judgment this consequential, we should state clearly what has failed and what we expect to change," he wrote. "This resolution falls short of that standard."

In a separate post ahead of the vote, Schaffer said that passage of a no confidence resolution would result in "no binding consequence."

data.title: U.S. Dollar Advances As Investors Analyze NFP Data Amid U.S.-Iran Stalemate
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Dollar value moved higher on Friday as the October nonfarm payrolls came in strongly above market forecasts while the unemployment rate slumped from September numbers. In addition, the U.S.-Iran conflict continues without an end in sight triggering inflation concerns.

Today, the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, which measures the Greenback against a basket of other major currencies, was last seen trading at 102.30, up by 0.72 (or 0.71%).

While against the Euro, the USD was trading at 1.114, up by 0.72%, against the GBP, the USD was trading at 1.335, up by 0.75%.

Against the USD, the Japanese Yen was trading at 158.527, down by 0.54% while the Swiss Franc was trading at 0.821, down by 0.53%.

Against the USD, the Canadian Dollar was trading at 1.413, down by 0.79%.

Statistics Canada today revealed that Canada's unemployment rate rose to 6.70% in October from 6.50% of September, reaching its highest level since April and above expectations that it would remain unchanged at 6.50%.

The labor force participation rate was unchanged at 64.8%, while employed persons fell by 4,700.

Against one unit of Australian Dollar, the USD was trading at 0.686, up by 0.95%.

In the U.S., On the economic front, the data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics revealed that the economy added 1,65,000 jobs in October, following an upwardly revised 60,000 increase in September, and well above market forecasts of 65,000. This is higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months.

The unemployment rate eased to 4.10% in October, down from 4.20% in September and slightly below market expectations of 4.20%.

Separately, the nonfarm payrolls private showed an addition of 1,59,000 in payrolls in October, the most in seven months following an upwardly revised 78,000 increase in September.

The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index rose to 51.00 in early November, up from 48.00 in October, and above market expectations of 48.00.

Yesterday, two officials of the U.S. Federal Reserve recommended a gradual ramping up of interest rates to combat inflation.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack stated that the Fed might need to move to adopt a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to the 2.00% level.

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin remarked that inflation is too high and added that steady rate hikes make sense.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, currently investors are betting on a 77.10% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike at the upcoming meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on December 8-9 while the odds on rates being held at the current level stand at 22.90%.

Investors are awaiting clarity on how the U.S. administration plans to defuse the Middle East crisis.

After the setback in the recently held mid-term elections, Trump remarked that Iran was partly responsible for the jolt.

Democrat-elects have to wait until January to assume office, offering a 60-day period for Trump to either choose diplomacy or military aggression as a tactic to deal with Iran.

Yesterday, Trump stated that the world will soon know his decision on the possibility of a deal with Iran. Declining to rule out military option, Trump maintained that he could also destroy what is left of Iran.

Reuters reported, citing an Iranian official that Iran had sent a nuclear proposal to the U.S. through Qatar.

Today, officially Qatar stated that the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani had a discussion with Trump over phone about de-escalation.

Amid this, the Strait of Hormuz continues to remain closed.

data.title: A Paradise Acquisition III Files for IPO
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

A Paradise III Acquisition filed for an initial public offering.

The special-purpose acquisition company plans to offer 10 million units for $10 apiece, where each unit consists of a share and one right that entitles the holder to receive a fourth of a share once the company acquires a business.

The company plans to look for an acquisition target in the leisure and entertainment sector.

A Paradise III is led by Claudius Tsang, who has led several other special-purpose acquisition companies. One of his SPACs bought Multimetaverse, an animation and entertainment company based in China.

A Paradise III plans to trade shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker APCD.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Canada's Big Rock Brewery Q3 net revenue falls due to sales volume drop
data.description:
Overview

  • Canada craft brewer's Q3 net revenue fell 10.4% as sales volumes dropped 21% yr/yr

  • Company reported negative adjusted EBITDA amid lower industry demand

  • Management cut workforce by 23% and reduced costs to align with lower revenues

Outlook

  • Company expects cost reductions to improve operating efficiency and future financial performance

  • Big Rock plans to increase focus on new warehousing and distribution revenue stream

Result Drivers

  • LOWER INDUSTRY DEMAND - Q3 sales volumes fell due to reduced contract and wholesale demand

  • WORKFORCE REDUCTION - Management cut workforce by 23% to align costs with lower sales volumes
